name: Recurrent Neural Networks and LSTM
description: Explore sequential deep learning architectures and understand how recurrent memory mechanisms function.

questions.question: What is the defining structural property of standard Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs)?
options: A hidden state fed back into the network across steps
A multi-head attention block replacing convolutions
A strictly feedforward path without any internal loops
A static document-term weighting matrix mechanism
questions.explain: RNNs maintain a recurring hidden state that passes prior step information forward to the current step.

questions.question: How do standard RNNs process an incoming natural language sentence?
options: By parsing all tokens in parallel using self-attention
By sequentially feeding one word at a time in order
By aggregating global word counts into static vectors
By shuffling tokens randomly into dense projection layers
questions.explain: RNNs iterate over input sequences step by step, updating their internal state on each word.

questions.question: Which major mathematical obstacle affects vanilla RNNs when processing long texts?
options: Vanishing Gradient
Deterministic Overfitting
Dimensionality Collapse
Greedy Token Pruning
questions.explain: Vanishing gradients cause vanilla RNNs to forget early contextual tokens as sequences grow long.

questions.question: What core component does an LSTM introduce to preserve long-term context?
options: A dynamic vocabulary stemmer
A static cross-entropy layer
A dedicated Cell State path
A positional sinusoidal matrix
questions.explain: The Cell State acts like a conveyor belt carrying long-term memory across sequential steps.

questions.question: Why did vanilla RNNs struggle with texts where the subject and predicate are far apart?
options: They discard word order entirely during text tokenization
They can only process numerical continuous financial data
They cannot maintain long-distance contextual dependencies
They require bidirectional Transformer decoders to run
questions.explain: Standard recurrent layers suffer from memory decay and fail to track long-range dependencies.

questions.question: What does the abbreviation LSTM stand for in deep learning terminology?
options: Linear Structured Text Modeling
Long Short-Term Memory
Latent Stochastic Tree Model
Layered Sequence Token Matrix
questions.explain: LSTM stands for Long Short-Term Memory, an architecture designed for long-term sequence tracking.

questions.question: What is the primary operational distinction between RNN working memory and LSTM design?
options: LSTM separates working memory from cell state memory
RNN relies completely on non-sequential matrix tensors
LSTM completely avoids calculating activation gradients
RNN eliminates recurrent connections between layers
questions.explain: LSTMs separate temporary working memory from long-term memory managed by the cell state.

questions.question: Which data type is inherently well-suited for processing by Recurrent Neural Networks?
options: Unordered tabular categories
Sequential and time-series data
Static spatial pixel matrices
Disjoint document vocabulary lists
questions.explain: Recurrent architectures are explicitly built to model sequential inputs and time-series signals.

questions.question: What hardware limitation hindered the massive scalability of RNN and LSTM models?
options: Inability to run on CPU arithmetic execution units
Requirement of quadratic GPU memory storage buffers
Sequential nature preventing efficient GPU parallelization
Strict dependency on single-precision integer caches
questions.explain: Step-by-step sequential processing prevents full parallel execution on modern GPU hardware.

questions.question: What architecture emerged directly to solve recurrent bottlenecks by processing sequences in parallel?
options: Multilayer Perceptron
Linear Discriminant Classifier
Latent Dirichlet Allocation
Transformer Model
questions.explain: Transformers replaced sequential recurrence with attention, allowing parallel sequence processing.
